instruments.short_name: Registration, Exemptions and Scale Based Regulation
instruments.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025
instruments.theme: Entry, structure and change of control
statutory_powers: Factoring Regulation Act 2011 s.3 r/w s.31A, s.6
applies_to: All NBFCs registered with RBI across Base, Middle, Upper and Top Layers, including Government NBFCs and HFCs
excluded: Entities exempted under Chapter IV, e.g. Nidhi, mutual benefit, chit, merchant banking, insurance companies, stock exchanges/brokers, AIF companies, ARCs, certain unregistered CICs
key_concepts: Layer test (paras 10-15, 24): BL = non-deposit NBFCs below ₹1,000 crore, plus NBFC-P2P, NBFC-AA, NOFHC and Type I NBFCs (always BL); ML = all NBFC-D, non-deposit NBFCs of ₹1,000 crore or more, SPD and IDF-NBFC (always ML); NBFC-D, CIC, NBFC-IFC and HFC sit in ML or UL, never BL; NBFC-ICC, MFI, Factor and MGC can sit in any layer by size; UL = NBFCs with assets of ₹1,00,000 crore or more on the latest audited balance sheet, identified annually by RBI; TL ideally empty

Amendments in the current text: SBR Amendment Directions 2026 (29-04-2026, in force 01-07-2026: Type I / Type II registration, exemption for NBFCs with no public funds and no customer interface) and Second Amendment Directions 2026 (24-06-2026: UL asset-size test, guidelines for NBFC group entities of banks)
core_obligations: para 17: aggregate assets of all NBFCs in a group / with common promoters to determine Middle Layer classification
para 20: statutory auditor to certify group-wide asset size as on 31 March every year and furnish to DoS
para 27(1): NBFC-UL to adopt Board-approved policy and implementation plan for the enhanced framework
para 27(3): submit Board-approved UL implementation roadmap to RBI
para 38A(2): Type I NBFCs seeking deregistration to apply through PRAVAAH with prescribed documents
para 38A(6): Type I NBFCs to disclose in Notes to Accounts that no public funds / customer interface were used; auditor exception report
para 43: NBFC not achieving prescribed NOF in time ceases to be eligible to hold CoR
para 47: no new investor from FATF non-compliant jurisdictions may acquire significant influence (20%+ voting power)
para 68: comply with reporting requirements prescribed by DoS
timelines: para 16: from 01-10-2022, references in earlier instructions to NBFC-ND are read as NBFC-BL, and to NBFC-D / NBFC-ND-SI as NBFC-ML or NBFC-UL (a reference-mapping rule, not the layer test)
para 20: annual group asset-size certificate (as on 31 March)
para 27(1): within 3 months of RBI advice of UL classification
para 27(2): up to 24 months from advice to comply with UL norms
para 28: stay in UL at least 5 years; exit only after 5 consecutive years below criteria
para 31: UL asset threshold reviewed every 3 years

para 38A(1): from 01-07-2026, NBFCs with no public funds and no customer interface and assets below ₹1,000 crore are exempt from s.45-IA and s.45-IC (para 65A); existing ones, incl. Type I NBFCs, may apply for deregistration by 31-12-2026

para 42-43: NOF glide path for existing NBFC-ICC (₹5 crore by 31-03-2025), NBFC-MFI and NBFC-Factor (₹7 crore by 31-03-2025) to ₹10 crore by 31-03-2027; NBFCs that miss it lose eligibility for the CoR
para 24: UL test is assets of ₹1,00,000 crore or more (substituted by the SBR Second Amendment Directions of 24-06-2026); para 22: ML rules apply as soon as a non-deposit NBFC reaches ₹1,000 crore
consequences_stated: para 38A(10): violation by unregistered Type I NBFC invites penal action under RBI Act 1934
para 43: failure to reach prescribed NOF makes the NBFC ineligible to hold CoR
instruments.consequences_general: Statutory consequences under the RBI Act 1934 (checked against the Act text as amended, 24-11-2026): RBI may impose a monetary penalty under s.58G: up to ₹25,000, or, for NBFI business without a CoR (s.58B(4A)) or for accepting deposits or not complying with a Chapter IIIB direction or order (s.58B(5)(a), (aa)), up to ₹10 lakh or twice the amount involved, whichever is more, plus up to ₹1 lakh a day while the default continues; a show-cause notice and hearing come first, and penalty and prosecution are alternatives (s.58G(2), (5)-(6)). As offences, s.58B(5) carries up to 3 years and fine, and s.58B(6) a fine up to ₹1 lakh plus ₹10,000 a day. RBI may also cancel the CoR (s.45-IA(6)), prohibit deposits or bar asset transfers (s.45MB), remove a director (s.45-ID), supersede the Board (s.45-IE) and petition for winding up (s.45MC). For HFCs the parallel provisions are NHB Act ss.29A(6), 49 and 52A (NHB or RBI may impose penalties, e.g. up to ₹10 lakh or twice the amount involved plus ₹1 lakh a day for not complying with a direction or order under Chapter V, s.52A(1C)).
instruments.repeals: Existing directions on registration, exemptions and SBR (incl. Master Direction – SBR 2023 and Master Circular on exemptions) repealed vide DOR.RRC.REC.302/33-01-010/2025-26 dated 28-11-2025

applies_to: NBFC-ML and above (D, ICC, Factor, MFI, IFC, IDF-NBFC), HFC, CIC
Credit bar on wilful defaulters applies to all regulated entities
excluded: NBFC-BL (cannot classify, but keeps reporting history)
key_concepts: Wilful default and wilful defaulter (≥ ₹25 lakh)
Natural justice: show-cause notice and hearing
core_obligations: para 4: Board policy on implementation
para 5(4): show-cause notice with 21 days to respond

para 5(7)-(11): written representation to the Review Committee within 15 days; opportunity of personal hearing (no right to a lawyer, as it is an in-house proceeding); reasoned order communicated to the wilful defaulter
para 5(14): non-executive/independent directors not classified unless complicity proven
para 6: examine all NPAs ≥ ₹25 lakh; classify within 6 months of NPA
para 7(3): no fresh credit to wilful defaulters; 1-year bar after delisting; 5-year bar on new ventures
para 11-12: monthly reporting of wilful and large defaulters to all CICs
para 14(1): examine wilful default before transferring loans ≥ ₹25 lakh
timelines: para 5(4): 21 days
para 5(7): 15 days
para 6(2): 6 months from NPA
para 11-12: monthly CIC reporting
para 12(2): delisting reported within 30 days
consequences_stated: para 7(3): penal measures (credit and new-venture bars) on the borrower

para 20-21: lender considers a complaint to NFRA / ICAI against a negligent statutory auditor of the borrower, forwarding it to RBI (DoS, CO) and IBA after a hearing; negligent third parties reported to IBA for its caution list; forensic audit above a Board-set threshold
instruments.consequences_general: Statutory consequences under the RBI Act 1934 (checked against the Act text as amended, 24-11-2026): RBI may impose a monetary penalty under s.58G: up to ₹25,000, or, for NBFI business without a CoR (s.58B(4A)) or for accepting deposits or not complying with a Chapter IIIB direction or order (s.58B(5)(a), (aa)), up to ₹10 lakh or twice the amount involved, whichever is more, plus up to ₹1 lakh a day while the default continues; a show-cause notice and hearing come first, and penalty and prosecution are alternatives (s.58G(2), (5)-(6)). As offences, s.58B(5) carries up to 3 years and fine, and s.58B(6) a fine up to ₹1 lakh plus ₹10,000 a day. RBI may also cancel the CoR (s.45-IA(6)), prohibit deposits or bar asset transfers (s.45MB), remove a director (s.45-ID), supersede the Board (s.45-IE) and petition for winding up (s.45MC). For HFCs the parallel provisions are NHB Act ss.29A(6), 49 and 52A (NHB or RBI may impose penalties, e.g. up to ₹10 lakh or twice the amount involved plus ₹1 lakh a day for not complying with a direction or order under Chapter V, s.52A(1C)).

instruments.title: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Chapter IIIB and penal provisions)
applies_to: All NBFCs (non-banking financial institutions) and their auditors (s.45-IA; s.45MA)

s.45-IA(1): Certificate of Registration and NOF of ₹25 lakh or such other amount, not exceeding ₹100 crore, as RBI notifies (different amounts for different categories allowed)
s.45-IB(1): invest in unencumbered approved securities at least 5% (or a higher rate up to 25% that RBI specifies) of deposits outstanding at the close of the second preceding quarter
s.45-IC: reserve fund; at least 20% of net profit each year before any dividend; appropriations only for RBI-specified purposes, reported to RBI within 21 days
s.45-IE: supersession of the Board of an NBFC (other than a Government company) for up to 5 years in all, with an Administrator
s.45K/45L power to collect information and give directions

s.45MC: RBI may petition for winding up if the NBFC cannot pay its debts, is disqualified under s.45-IA, has been barred from deposits by an order in force for 3 months or more, or its continuance harms the public or depositors; deemed unable to pay debts if it fails to meet a lawful demand within 5 working days and RBI certifies this
s.45QA NCLT order to repay deposits
s.45-ID: removal of a director of an NBFC (other than a Government-owned NBFC) by a reasoned RBI order after a chance to make a representation
core_obligations: s.45-IA(1): obtain a Certificate of Registration and hold the minimum NOF before commencing or carrying on NBFI business
Maintain liquid assets on public deposits (s.45-IB)
s.45-IC(1): transfer at least 20% of net profit, as shown in the P&L, to a reserve fund every year before any dividend is declared
ss.45JA, 45K, 45L, 45M: comply with RBI directions and furnish the statements and information RBI calls for
s.45QA: repay every deposit on its terms unless renewed; the Tribunal (formerly the Company Law Board) may order repayment on its own motion or on a depositor's application
timelines: Reserve fund transfer every year before dividend
Returns/information as RBI directs
s.45-IC(2): report each appropriation from the reserve fund to RBI within 21 days of the withdrawal
s.45-IA(7): appeal against rejection or cancellation of the CoR to the Central Government within 30 days of the order being communicated
s.58G(3): pay an RBI penalty within 30 days of the demand notice, failing which it is recovered through the civil court
consequences_stated: s.45-IA(6): cancellation of the CoR if the NBFC stops NBFI business, breaches a CoR condition, fails the s.45-IA(4)(d)-(g) conditions, fails to comply with directions, keep accounts or produce books, or has been barred from deposits by an order in force for 3 months or more; chance to comply and a hearing first
s.45MB: prohibition on accepting deposits; bar on selling, transferring or charging assets for up to 6 months

Winding-up petition (s.45MC)

Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 (8 of 2026; assent 07-04-2026), in force for the RBI Act from 23-06-2026 (S.O. 3301(E) of 22-06-2026): s.58B(4AA) omitted; s.58B heading changed to 'Offences' and s.58G heading to 'penalties' (Schedule serial 7). consequences_stated: s.21: default in filing assignment or realisation particulars under s.19, penalty on the factor and every officer in default of up to ₹5 lakh plus up to ₹10,000 a day, imposed by RBI under s.22(2)-(4); s.22(1): not complying with an RBI direction under s.6, penalty up to ₹5 lakh plus up to ₹10,000 a day; show-cause notice and hearing first (s.22(2)); payable within 14 days of the demand notice (s.22(3)); s.23: other contraventions, up to 1 year, or fine, or both; s.24: cognizance only on a complaint by an authorised RBI officer

instruments.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and FSP Rules, 2019
applies_to: NBFCs as financial creditors of borrowers

NBFCs (incl. HFCs) with assets of ₹500 crore or more in the last audited balance sheet, notified as FSPs under s.227 (S.O. 4139(E) of 18-11-2019, RBI as appropriate regulator): CIRP only on RBI's application, treated as a s.7 application, with an Administrator (FSP Rules 2019, G.S.R. 852(E) of 15-11-2019, r.5(a)); creditors cannot file under ss.7/9 and the NBFC cannot file under s.10
core_obligations: Use IBC as a resolution route; align with RBI stressed-assets framework
timelines: s.12: CIRP within 180 days, one extension of up to 90 days on a 66% CoC vote, outer limit 330 days including litigation time, subject to judicial exceptions (Essar Steel, 2019)

FSP Rules r.5: interim moratorium from the filing of RBI's application; the FSP's licence or registration is not suspended or cancelled during CIRP; an advisory committee may be set up within 45 days; the regulator's no-objection for the resolution plan is deemed given if not refused within 45 working days
consequences_stated: Moratorium and resolution outcomes; RBI-initiated insolvency of FSPs (FSP Rules r.5); regulator heard before liquidation (r.7); voluntary liquidation of an FSP needs the regulator's prior permission (r.8)

instruments.short_name: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act
instruments.title: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
applies_to: Deposit-takers including NBFCs (regulated schemes outside the ban if compliant)
core_obligations: s.3: no deposit taker may promote, operate, advertise or accept deposits under an unregulated deposit scheme; s.4: no fraudulent default in repaying deposits under a regulated deposit scheme
consequences_stated: s.21: soliciting under an unregulated scheme, 1-5 years and ₹2-10 lakh; accepting, 2-7 years and ₹3-10 lakh; accepting with fraudulent default, 3-10 years and ₹5 lakh up to twice the amounts collected; s.22: fraudulent default under a regulated scheme (s.4), up to 7 years, or fine of ₹5 lakh-₹25 crore or three times the profit made, whichever is higher, or both; s.23: wrongful inducement (s.5), 1-5 years and up to ₹10 lakh

instruments.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (not an RBI law; impacts NBFCs)
applies_to: NBFCs as data fiduciaries (digital lending, KYC, AA)
key_concepts: s.44(2)(a): omits IT Act s.43A once that provision commences (13-05-2027)
core_obligations: Process personal data with valid consent and purpose limitation

s.8: a Data Fiduciary is accountable for its processors, must take reasonable security safeguards (8(5)), tell the Board and each affected Data Principal of a personal data breach (8(6)), and erase data once the purpose is served (8(7))
timelines: Commencement (G.S.R. 843(E) of 13-11-2025): definitions, the Board and procedural provisions from 13-11-2025; Consent Manager provisions (s.6(9), s.27(1)(d)) from 13-11-2026; the main obligations (ss.3-17 incl. s.8), penalties (s.33) and the omission of IT Act s.43A from 13-05-2027

DPDP Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E) of 13-11-2025): r.4 (Consent Managers) after one year; rr.3, 5-16, 22, 23 after eighteen months; r.7(2): tell the Board of a breach without delay and send a detailed report within 72 hours
consequences_stated: s.33 and Schedule (from 13-05-2027), imposed by the Data Protection Board after inquiry into a significant breach: security safeguards (s.8(5)) up to ₹250 crore; breach intimation (s.8(6)) up to ₹200 crore; children's data (s.9) up to ₹200 crore; Significant Data Fiduciary duties (s.10) up to ₹150 crore; any other provision up to ₹50 crore

instruments.title: Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026
instruments.theme: Allied RBI instruments (FEMA, markets, payments, ombudsman)
statutory_powers: UNVERIFIED: statutory basis not checked (the Scheme text could not be fetched)
applies_to: NBFCs registered with RBI that are authorised to accept deposits, or have a customer interface and assets of ₹100 crore or more on the previous year's audited balance sheet (FAQ Q13)
Excluded: HFC, CIC, IDF-NBFC, NBFC-IFC, NOFHC, Primary Dealers, MGC (FAQ Q13)
key_concepts: Complaint must first go to the NBFC, with proof (FAQ Q16, Q17)
No limit on the amount in dispute (FAQ Q22)
Compensation up to ₹30 lakh for consequential loss, plus up to ₹3 lakh for loss of time, expenses, harassment and mental anguish (FAQ Q22-23; the 2021 Scheme had ₹20 lakh + ₹1 lakh)
Appeal lies only against an Award; no appeal for the NBFC against an Award passed for its failure to furnish information (FAQ Q31)
Complaints received before 01-07-2026, appeals under RB-IOS 2021 and execution of its awards stay under the 2021 Scheme (FAQ Q1)
An authorised representative cannot be an advocate unless the advocate is the aggrieved person (FAQ Q20)
core_obligations: Customer may approach the Ombudsman after the NBFC's reply, or after 30 days (or any longer time under RBI, NPCI or card-network rules) with no reply (FAQ Q17)
NBFC must comply with the Award and report compliance, or appeal with prior sanction, within 30 days of receiving the complainant's letter of acceptance (FAQ Q29, Q31-32)
timelines: 30 days (or longer time under RBI, NPCI or card-network rules) for the NBFC to reply before escalation (FAQ Q17)
90 days for the customer to approach the Ombudsman, from expiry of that period or the NBFC's last communication, whichever is later; the complaint to the NBFC must be within limitation (FAQ Q17)
30 days for the NBFC to comply with the Award or appeal, from receipt of the complainant's acceptance (FAQ Q29)
30 days for the complainant to accept the Award, or to appeal; the Appellate Authority may allow up to 30 more days (FAQ Q29, Q32)
consequences_stated: Award directing remedial action and/or compensation against the NBFC, after both sides are heard (FAQ Q24, Q28)
cross_references: Directions whose text (as updated) still names RB-IOS 2021: P2P para 53, AA para 40, Outsourcing para 57, Credit Cards para 79(2), Financial Statements (complaints disclosure note); Credit Information Reporting para 35-36 refers to the Scheme 'as amended'

instruments.title: Master Direction – Foreign Investment in India

instruments.title: Master Direction – External Commercial Borrowings, Trade Credits and Structured Obligations
